rows.reasoning: The record's configuration is defined as exactly this published apparatus. Section III.2 enumerates every detector on the 116 mm x 140 mm cryogenic breadboard (QPD for beam position, high-bandwidth PD for reflection, photodiode for transmission) and the room-temperature InGaAs camera outside the cryostat; Fig. 5 legend lists the same parts. The apparatus is an optical frequency reference (abstract: 'A system providing an optical frequency with an instability comparable to that of a hydrogen maser'), interrogated at 100 nW-1 uW with analog photodiodes. No superconducting nanowire single-photon detector, bias or readout electronics is part of it; a full-text search of the paper for 'nanowire', 'single-photon', 'SNSPD' found nothing. This is scope-based absence from the positive component description, not silence.

Timing here is optical-frequency metrology, not photon arrival-time measurement; a 40 kS/s analog sampler is not a TCSPC or time-tagging instrument. The paper's own description of the apparatus therefore positively establishes there is no photon-timing module. rows.value_as_printed: Optical frequency reference interrogated at 100 nW - 1.3 uW; no calibrated attenuation path or detector-under-test characterization setup
rows.quote: A system providing an optical frequency with an instability comparable to that of a hydrogen maser is presented. It consists of a 5 cm long, vertically oriented silicon optical resonator operated at temperatures between 1.5 K and 3.6 K in a closed-cycle cryostat with low-temperature Joule-Thomson stage.

rows.reasoning: The vocabulary defines this key as an installed calibrated optical power measurement and attenuation path for detector characterization. The paper positively describes the apparatus as an optical frequency reference (silicon resonator interrogated by a ULE-prestabilized laser through a fiber, AOM and free-space breadboard) and enumerates its full optical chain; there is no detector under test and no calibrated attenuator chain to deliver a known single-photon-level flux. The paper does report incident interrogation powers (200 nW, 1.3 uW, 520 nW, 550-100 nW, about 1 mW during PDH alignment), so laser power was monitored, but that is resonator-interrogation power, not a calibrated photon-flux source for detector characterization.
